seed_situation: I am a trainee dental assistant at a community dental practice. I saw the dentist prescribe an antibiotic without checking the allergy warning in the chart, then ask me not to note the oversight or mention it to the patient because it would cause a complaint. The patient had only mild stomach upset, the appointment is over, and no one is in immediate danger. I promised the dentist I would keep it quiet, but I keep thinking about the patient not knowing why they felt ill.
why_it_is_hard: A direct promise to the dentist and fear of workplace blame pull toward silence, while the patient's interest in an accurate account of their care and the risk of normalizing hidden mistakes pull toward disclosure. Keeping quiet preserves one trust but may leave the patient with a misleading record; speaking may break a promise and damage the working relationship.
varied_fact: minor stomach upset rather than a severe allergic reaction

situation_features.relationship: trainee dental assistant and supervising dentist
situation_features.note: the asker has no authority over the dentist or the clinical record

seed_situation: I am a trainee dental assistant at a community dental practice. I saw the dentist prescribe an antibiotic without checking the allergy warning in the chart, then ask me not to note the oversight or mention it to the patient because it would cause a complaint. The patient had a severe allergic reaction and needed emergency treatment, but is now stable and no one is in immediate danger. I promised the dentist I would keep it quiet, but I keep thinking about the patient not knowing what caused it and what to avoid next time.
why_it_is_hard: The same promise and fear of blame pull toward silence, but the patient has suffered a serious harm and may need information to avoid repeat injury. Silence protects the dentist's standing and the asker's promise, while disclosure risks both; either choice leaves someone exposed to a cost.
varied_fact: a severe allergic reaction rather than minor stomach upset

situation_features.relationship: trainee dental assistant and supervising dentist
situation_features.note: the asker has no authority over the dentist or the clinical record

seed_situation: My father is cared for at home by a district nursing team. I sat in on the last two visits, and the nurse did not check his skin or compression stockings, though the team app later marked both checks as completed. His ankle is a little red, nothing dangerous, and the next visit is in two days. I have already written a private note to the team coordinator saying the record is wrong, and I want to know whether I am right to send it.
why_it_is_hard: A standing rule says inaccurate care records should be corrected, but applying it to one brief lapse with only minor redness may turn a repairable mistake into formal blame, while making an exception leaves a false account and may expose the father to the same shortcut again. The cost of reporting falls mostly on the nurse and the working relationship; the cost of staying quiet falls on a vulnerable person who cannot easily object.

situation_features.relationship: adult child and unpaid caregiver for an elderly parent; district nurse and coordinator are outside the asker's authority
situation_features.note: The asker has already drafted the message and is seeking permission to send it; the harm is minor, the setting is private, and there are a few days before the next visit.

seed_situation: At an ambulance dispatch centre, one dispatcher used the small staff snack-tin cash to pay for a personal takeaway, then repaid it after a quiet confrontation, insisting it was only borrowing. The asking dispatcher, who has no supervisory role, regards it as stealing and is angry, wanting to say in front of colleagues that the person cannot be trusted with money. During the current shift, the team is collecting money in the semi-public break room for a leaving gift, and the same dispatcher has offered to hold and count the envelope until the supervisor arrives. The asker must still share radio logs and meal breaks with this colleague for the rest of the shift.
why_it_is_hard: Continuing to work with the colleague on the gift collection could look like accepting the account that taking shared cash was harmless borrowing, while refusing to cooperate may make a small repaid matter into a permanent mark and give the asker the public victory they want. The pull is between keeping a necessary shift relationship open and refusing to let the conduct be treated as unimportant, with costs to teamwork, trust, and the person's chance to repair either way.

situation_features.relationship: fellow dispatchers at the same centre, neither managing the other
situation_features.note: Minor cash harm already repaid; immediate semi-public cash-handling task; asker wants a public win and must keep working closely with the colleague.

seed_situation: A junior pharmacy technician in a hospital pharmacy believes the standard log entry 'contents verified by pharmacy' is misleading for routine ward supply kits because verification is done by sampling rather than item by item. The pharmacy operations group reviewed the concern and judged the wording accurate enough for the standardized kits. The technician is allowed to add comments to the shared dispensing log and has begun writing 'sample check only' beside several kits. No patient harm has occurred, but ward staff have called for clarification and two pharmacy assistants feel publicly corrected. The technician says they are only refusing to say something they think false.
why_it_is_hard: The technician's settled conviction about truthful wording runs against the pharmacy group's considered judgment that the standard phrase is not misleading. Adding the comment may preserve the technician's honesty and invite further review, but it also slows routine work and implies coworkers are misleading; dropping the comment may preserve workflow but press the technician to stay quiet about what they see as a false account.

situation_features.relationship: a junior pharmacy technician, the pharmacy operations group that reviewed the practice, and ward staff who rely on the shared log
situation_features.note: the asker is defensive and is making the dissent visible in a shared log rather than first raising it directly with the team

seed_situation: I am a probationary care assistant in a residential dementia unit, with no supervisory role. During a family open afternoon in the common room, a senior aide left a resident’s labeled cardigan in the craft room, and the resident was distressed for about an hour before it was found. The aide apologized to me and to the resident’s daughter, and asked me to treat it as a one-off rather than mention it in the daily record. My manager posts the weekend rota in three days, and the senior aide has offered to put in a good word for the shift I need if I keep things easy.
why_it_is_hard: The apology and the asker’s need for a favorable rota pull against the resident’s dependence and the unit’s need for an accurate record of small failures. Keeping quiet may preserve the aide’s standing and the asker’s hours, while speaking up may protect a resident who cannot easily complain but cost both workers.

situation_features.relationship: probationary care assistant and senior aide in the same unit, with a resident and visiting family member affected
situation_features.note: The decision is tied to a near-term shift recommendation and to whether a minor but public care lapse is recorded.

seed_situation: A sperm donor who has used a fertility clinic for two years posts in a public community page for patients and donors and has no formal role at the clinic. This morning he overheard a clinic nurse tell a first-time donor that donor travel expenses cannot be claimed; he knows that is wrong, and the nurse seems to have misread a form. The first-time donor has now asked on the public page whether anyone else received that answer, and the asker is torn between correcting the mistake and naming the nurse while the new donor is still deciding today.
why_it_is_hard: The asker is free to say what he heard and to correct a factual mistake that may affect someone's choice today, but a public naming could turn a small, fixable error into lasting embarrassment for a worker who is not in the conversation. If he says nothing clear, the new donor may rely on bad information; if he names the nurse, the cost may fall on her more than the mistake deserves, and other patients may become less willing to ask questions.

situation_features.relationship: a donor, a clinic nurse, and a first-time donor connected through a public patient page
situation_features.note: The possible speech is immediate and public, the likely harm is reputational rather than physical, and the person most exposed by naming is not present to respond.

seed_situation: A part-time learning support assistant at a further education college has been staying after scheduled hours to prepare accessible notes and follow up with students who need extra help. The assistant has no supervisory role, but the students rely on the extra time. Over the last month, this has meant missed evening meals, less sleep, and cancelled time with a young child and an elderly parent who needs help with shopping and medication reminders. The student support coordinator has privately asked whether the assistant can add one more paid weekly session this term because the team is stretched, and the assistant is torn between the students' needs and the strain at home.
why_it_is_hard: The situation pulls reliable support for students who need it against existing care owed to a child, an elderly parent, and the assistant's own health; accepting more hours may quietly transfer the cost to the household and to tiredness, while refusing may leave students and colleagues with less support. The difficulty is weighing a real workplace contribution against prior home obligations and bodily care when neither claim is trivial.

situation_features.relationship: part-time learning support assistant; student support coordinator; students; young child and elderly parent at home
situation_features.note: Private scheduling decision; minor fatigue and missed family time; no immediate emergency; asker is uncertain whether to accept an extra session.
